elements.title: Waterloo Column (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Waterloo Column (pictured), which commemorates Germans who died at the Battle of Waterloo, incorporates the barrels of eight cannons that were captured there?

elements.title: Harold Styan (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that gym teacher Harold Styan of Clifton House School was appointed Officer of the Order of the British Empire for services to youth?

elements.title: Life Till Bones (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that one critic described some of the melodies in Life Till Bones as akin to "trying to dig a hole in a bowl full of sugar"?

elements.title: Goro Takahashi (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Goro Takahashi, a silversmith adopted by a Lakota family, was the first Japanese person allowed to attend a Sun Dance?

elements.title: a Rhode Island TV station (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a Rhode Island TV station started out by re-running an inventory of 50 hours of cartoons and 14 old movies?

elements.title: Zhang Xinsheng (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the 1923 film Zhang Xinsheng featured close-up views of internal organs?

elements.title: marzēaḥ (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that an inscription from 243 AD for a leader of the marzēaḥ ends with blessings for his sons, the scribe, the person in charge of the cooking, the cupbearer, and other assistants?

elements.title: Ripken (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Ripken wore a GoPro on his back while retrieving used bats and tees at major sporting events?

elements.title: latest album (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that trucks in Tyler promoted Tyler's latest album?
